cadence_anomaly_GRID_SCORING_ARTIFACT.flag: FLAGGED -- a real, important measurement finding (NOT a survivor).
cadence_anomaly_GRID_SCORING_ARTIFACT.observation: As the combo grid fines (1d->4h->2h->1h), PBO DROPS (0.71->0.21->0.25->0.08) and raw xBH RISES (some combos exceed 1.0xBH; at 1h the best non-redundant combo shows oos_xbh=2.05, iron_xbh=2.70, and even a POSITIVE p05_vs_bh_oos=+13.0). This is the OPPOSITE of the prior expectation (finer = more churn = PBO stays HIGH).
cadence_anomaly_GRID_SCORING_ARTIFACT.root_cause: GRID-SCORING ARTIFACT, not edge. _combo_book applies the lag-1 at the COMBO cadence (pos=held_lead[:-1], combinatrix.py:222), so a coarse-native signal (e.g. CKSP@1d) ffilled onto a fine combo grid silently reacts ~23h FASTER at every flip (a hidden change of execution latency), compounded by a within-day Jensen term on partial-exposure days. The strategy's TRIGGERS are identical across grids (same n_trades=4.7, same time_in~0.31) but its FILLS are re-clocked finer.
cadence_anomaly_GRID_SCORING_ARTIFACT.proof_1_same_strategy_inflates: CKSP@1d single, IDENTICAL trades/exposure on every grid: OOS net 20.1(1d)/43.3(4h)/51.3(1h); Sharpe 2.39/4.11/4.62. GROSS (no vol-target, no cost): 24.2/52.2/59.9 -- so the inflation is NOT cost and NOT vol-target.
cadence_anomaly_GRID_SCORING_ARTIFACT.proof_2_falsifier_restores_invariance: Re-score with the lag-1 applied at the NATIVE 1d cadence (ffill the ALREADY-lagged position) -> gross OOS is GRID-INVARIANT: 24.2/24.1/24.9/25.6 across 1d/4h/2h/1h (residual ~6% = benign within-day Jensen). This isolates the artifact to the combo-cadence lag exactly as predicted.
cadence_anomaly_GRID_SCORING_ARTIFACT.proof_3_anomaly_combo_is_artifact: OR(KELTNER@4h+ADX@4h) (both 4h-native) scored across grids: oos_xbh 0.295(1d)/0.685(4h-its-native)/1.589(2h)/2.051(1h); p05_vs_bh_oos -63.1/-45.5/-5.3/+13.0. At its HONEST 4h native cadence it LOSES to BH by a mile (p05=-45.5); the +13 p05 at 1h is purely the finer-grid re-clock. p05 vs best-single stays NEGATIVE (-7.7) even at 1h, and robust=False at 1h.
cadence_anomaly_GRID_SCORING_ARTIFACT.differential_favoring: The artifact flatters IN/OUT strategies (flips + partial exposure) and is ZERO for always-in buy-hold (pos==1 -> daily compounding is grid-invariant). So xBH is NOT apples-to-apples across cadences: BH inflates only +21% (32.5->39.4, pure Jensen) while the trend single inflates +155% (20.1->51.3). The xBH crossover above 1.0 is a metric artifact, not a real beat.
implications: The finer-cadence xBH numbers MUST carry a heavy caveat -- do NOT report 'combo beats BH at 1h' as real edge.
PBO=0.08 at 1h is CONTAMINATED (the grid-stable artifact dilutes the IS->OOS rank-instability PBO measures); do NOT cite it as robustness.

The 0-survivor verdict is UNAFFECTED and HONEST: White's RC (built on the same grid, deflated by M) + the negative p05-vs-single + IRON-confirm catch the artifact at every cadence. The gate worked two-sided.

For honest cross-cadence comparison of a coarse-native input, the lag must be applied at the NATIVE TF BEFORE ffill, not at the combo cadence after (combinatrix.py:222). This is the one code note worth a future fix; it does not change THIS null.
